newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait firm, Citibank to fund jet fuel purchase.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait firm, Citibank to fund jet fuel purchase.

text.p: Kuwait Finance House (KFH) and Citibank are nearing a deal to finance the purchase of up to $100 million worth of jet fuel for the Malaysian Airline Systems Bhd (MAS), KFH said on Monday.
"The contract is in its final stages. It will be ready in about two days," said an official at KFH's foreign investment department.
"The House's part of the deal would be $50 million and Citibank would be the underwriter for the rest. There could be other banks under Citibank," said the official.
Under the deal KFH and co-financers would buy jet fuel from suppliers and sell it on to MAS at a profit in several transactions over three months following the signing.

MAS will settle each transaction a year after the original purchase with a deferred payment to the financers. The official did not disclose the profit on the purchases, but he said "they would be in line with the prices on the Malaysian markets."
The deal is structured under the rules of Murabaha, an Islamic banking method designed to avert interest payments. Islamic banking does not allow interest on lending.
Under Murabaha financial institutions buy goods in agreement with a client and sell them on to him at a profit.
The volume of fuel the banks will buy for MAS is not fixed. Under the term of the agreement the $100 million figure is the maximum the banks may spend on buying fuel.
